newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA PRIVATISATION AGENCY TO SELL ANIMAL FARMS.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA PRIVATISATION AGENCY TO SELL ANIMAL FARMS.

text.p: Romania's main privatisation agency said on Tuesday it would call tenders later this month to privatise 20 poultry and pig raising farms.
"The State Ownership Fund (FPS) will put on sale the stake it has in each of these companies, which ranges from 51 to 70 percent," FPS official Marius Aposteanu told Reuters.
Liquidation procedures will be launched for the farms the FPS does not manage to sell, he added.
On offer are small, medium and big farms, with share capital bases ranging from around 8.0 to 64 billion lei.
"Around 30 percent of the 20 farms are sound companies, the rest more or less face financial difficulties," Aposteanu said.
Local economists hailed the move as a sign of the commitment to faster reforms of the new government, which came to power after general elections last November.
"You have to start somewhere and agriculture is a good sector to start with," an economist said.

The former leftist government had been frequently accused of stalling reforms and delaying privatisation. Since late 1992 when it was created, the FPS has managed to privatise around 3,000 of the 6,500 companies in its portfolio.

In a separate mass selloff, Romanians could swap coupons for stakes of up to 60 percent in some 4,000 companies. Subscription was a massive 90 percent, but economists said the scheme still left the bulk of the economy in state hands.

The new government coalition -- grouping mainly centrists and social democrats -- announced last month radical reforms, including faster privatisation and restructuring, in exchange for renewed credits from international lenders.

Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea recently told Western businessmen at a Bucharest conference on investment opportunities that Romania was planning to privatise banks, communications, utilities and oil companies. "If you are interested to invest in such areas you're welcome," he said.
Direct foreign investments in Romania since the fall of communism in 1989 stood at a little over $2.0 billion at end-1996, a level far below elsewhere in Eastern Europe. ($=7,744 lei)
